new.name: Transcript paragraphs turned into a table on some pages and a list on others
new.page_shows: Numbered transcript paragraphs 988-997, each with a bold speaker name, laid out in the same way as every other page
new.output_says: | 988. | ELDER JOSEPHINE THOMAS BREMNER: (Speaking in Native language). | (page 46 of the same document renders the same layout as '- 974. ELDER JOANNE GLADEAU: ...' list items)
new.why_it_matters: Paragraph number and speaker land in table cells on some pages and in list items on others; a parser keyed on '- NNN. SPEAKER:' misses whole pages, and a table-aware reader treats the speech as data rows
new.lesson: Treat numbered transcript paragraphs as one structure regardless of how the page was detected; normalise table-vs-list in a transcript post-pass

new.name: Margin line numbers and time codes kept as running text in transcripts
new.page_shows: A court-reporter page with line numbers 1-25 and a time code (04:01:00 ...) in the left margin, and text lines hard-wrapped to the line grid
new.output_says:
1  04:01:00 questions.
2  04:01:01 PRESIDING COMMISSIONER KATHY PENNEY: Thanks very
3  04:01:04 much.
new.why_it_matters: Every line starts with a line number and a time code, so sentences are cut into 25 fragments per page, speaker turns and paragraph breaks are not marked, and chunking/embedding mixes digits and time stamps into the prose; the margin numbers are page furniture used only for citing, yet they read as content
new.lesson: Recognise a transcript page: strip margin numbers and time codes into line metadata, rejoin wrapped lines, start a new block at each speaker label
